# 06 — Sidebar navigation (automatic and manual)

## What Antora does natively

Every valid `.adoc` under `modules/<module>/pages/` can become a published page. **Antora shows links in its sidebar only when they are present in a registered navigation file.** This project supplies an optional generator for that file.

## Option A — Automatically generated navigation

Make sure `antora.yml` includes:

```yaml
nav:
  - modules/ROOT/nav-generated.adoc
```

From the directory containing `antora.yml` and `modules/`:

```powershell
python tools/generate_nav.py --content-root .
antora antora-playbook.yaml
```

For `docs/antora.yml`, run `--content-root docs` instead.

### Current generator grouping rules (verified)

The provided Python script scans **all module** `pages/**/*.adoc` files. It groups by the leading folder name when there is a subfolder, otherwise by module name. Folder-name aliases are mapped as follows:

| Folder alias | Sidebar heading |
|---|---|
| `lld`, `low-level-design` | Low-Level Design |
| `hld`, `high-level-design` | High-Level Design |
| `engineering-notes`, `notes`, `systems`, `backend`, `devops` | Engineering Notes |
| Other folder/module names (`java`, etc.) | Other Articles |

It writes `modules/ROOT/nav-generated.adoc`; creates the target folder if necessary; prioritizes `:page-navtitle:` over the page's `= Title`; skips `modules/ROOT/pages/index.adoc`; skips pages containing `:page-nav-exclude:` in their initial header lines; and sorts files by path.

It **does not** recreate deep folder nesting or honor arbitrary manual heading hierarchies. If you need categories like `Garbage Collection > GC Types > G1`, use a manual nav file or extend the generator.

### Example generated output

```asciidoc
// Generated by tools/generate_nav.py — do not hand edit
* Low-Level Design
** xref:ROOT:lld/parking-lot.adoc[Parking Lot]
* High-Level Design
** xref:ROOT:hld/url-shortener.adoc[URL Shortener]
* Other Articles
** xref:java:index.adoc[Garbage Collection]
```

## Option B — Hand-maintained nested navigation

Create `modules/ROOT/nav.adoc`:

```asciidoc
* Garbage Collection
** xref:java:index.adoc[Introduction]
** GC Algorithms
*** xref:java:garbage-collection/g1-gc.adoc[G1 Garbage Collector]
* Low-Level Design
** xref:ROOT:lld/parking-lot.adoc[Parking Lot]
* High-Level Design
** xref:ROOT:hld/url-shortener.adoc[URL Shortener]
* Contact
** xref:java:contact.adoc[Contact Details]
```

Then in `antora.yml`:

```yaml
nav:
  - modules/ROOT/nav.adoc
```

Do **not** run the generator expecting it to alter `nav.adoc`. This mode gives you full control over ordering and nested list depth (Antora supports up to five list levels in navigation files).

## Combining manual and generated nav

Register both when useful:

```yaml
nav:
  - modules/ROOT/nav.adoc
  - modules/ROOT/nav-generated.adoc
```

But ensure the generator won't include pages also listed manually, or the sidebar can show duplicates. A safe approach is to choose one method first, then deliberately divide page ownership if needed.

## Header configuration page should not appear

`header-links.adoc` begins with:

```asciidoc
:page-nav-exclude:
```

**This is a convention in our generator only.** Antora itself still publishes the file as a page. For manual nav, just omit it from the nav list.

## Empty/missing category names

Use explicit, nonempty parent labels in nav files:

```asciidoc
* Architecture Diagrams
** xref:java:architecture.adoc[Architecture Overview]
```

The current UI defensively replaces empty parent labels with a child title when possible. This fallback is not a substitute for correct navigation source text. The category buttons remain readable when collapsed and preserve compact spacing.

## Link vs collapsible category

The UI renders a **nonlinked category with children** as a button that opens/closes. A **linked parent with children** is rendered as a link with visible nested links; current template behavior is not guaranteed to offer a separate accordion toggle for that parent. For expandable categories, use plain text for the parent (`* Low-Level Design`) and `xref` on the children.

## Browser filter behavior

`Filter pages...` filters **sidebar navigation labels** on the current page. It is **not full-site text search**. To add full-text indexing, integrate a search service or extension separately.
